title: Emergency burst paths — procurement sensitivity sim
content:
Purpose:
Short working simulation to evaluate emergency "burst" procurement paths (fast vendors, short-term leases, cross-region reflows) and TTL (time-to-fulfill) sensitivity across SKU mixes for a 12-week high-demand window. Goal is to produce a prioritized set of actionable procurement lanes and a quick checklist for on-call infra/ops if we hit >125% normal burn for 2+ days.

High-level summary:
- We model four procurement lanes: reserved orders (standard commit), brokered short-term leases (spot+lease brokers), vendor fast-ship (premium paid, ~2–4 week lead), and cross-region pull (reallocate existing inventory across regions).
- Key axes: lead time distribution, max deployable units per week, cost multiplier, compatibility (model support), and risk of failure.
- Simulation runs 10k Monte Carlo draws over demand shock distributions (mild, medium, severe).

Assumptions (inputs):
- Typical baseline weekly burn: 4k GPU-weeks globally (all regions).
- Shock scenarios: mild (+25%), medium (+60%), severe (+120%).
- SKUs in play: H100-80GB (H100), A100-80GB (A100), L40-40GB (L40).
- Region lead time baselines (days): us-west: 35, us-east: 30, eu-west: 45, apac: 60.
- Fast-ship vendor typical lead: 14–28 days, max 1.5k units per order.
- Broker lease: 7–21 days activation, variable returns, up to 2k units/week but only 70% compatible for LLM serving.
- Cross-region pull: 0–7 days internal transfer but limited by local SLAs and 30% operational friction.

Quick formulas used in the sim (verbatim):
- demand_t = baseline_weekly * (1 + shock_pct)
- committed_capacity_t = reserved_inventory_on_hand + scheduled_arrivals_within_ttl_days
- expected_shortfall_t = max(0, demand_t - committed_capacity_t - leased_capacity_t - pulled_capacity_t)
- cost_of_fill = sum(unit_cost_lane * units_acquired_lane) + premium_fees + expedited_fees

Scenario results (12-week sim, aggregated):
CSV table (scenario,probability,median_shortfall_gpu-weeks,90th_pct_shortfall,preferred_lane,recommended_order):
"Mild (25%)",0.62,120,350,broker-lease,"lease 1.5k H100-equivalent (4 weeks)"
"Medium (60%)",0.31,680,1,450,fast-vendor+broker,"order 1.2k H100 fast-ship + 1.0k broker lease"
"Severe (120%)",0.07,2,400,5,200,hybrid-burst,"immediate 1.5k fast-vendor, 3.0k broker lease staggered w/ cross-region pulls"

(Notes: CSV rows intentionally flattened; numbers are illustrative from the sim run seeded on 2024-11-01.)

Per-lane profile (short):
- Reserved orders: predictable, cheapest unit price, long lead ~30–60d, no premium. Good for baseline replenishment only.
- Broker lease: fast-ish, mid-price, availability uncertain, useful for smoothing 2–8 week shocks. Compatibility rate varies by SKU.
- Fast-ship vendor: expensive (1.8–2.5x), reliable within capacity caps, best for immediate 2–6 week fills.
- Cross-region pull: cost low (internal transfer), constrained by SLA and 0.6x usable capacity after friction. Best as first-response where inventory exists.

SKU sensitivity note:
- H100 density: highest performance/cost ratio for our large-chat workloads; shortages here cause highest SLA risk.
- A100 is acceptable fallback for many workloads (quantized) but increases token-cost and latency.
- L40 useful for embedding/low-attention workloads but cannot replace H100 for high-throughput chat.

Sample numeric extract — lead time sensitivity (H100 only):
Table: lead_time_days -> median_shortfall_gpu-weeks (medium shock)
- 14 days: 120
- 21 days: 300
- 35 days: 620
- 60 days: 1,200
Interpretation: Getting lead time below ~21 days via brokers/fast-vendor meaningfully reduces risk.

Decision checklist for on-call (quick deploy):
1) T0 (trigger: 2 consecutive days >125% burn): open JIRA-INFRA-EMERG and ping procurement on-call (Aisha).
2) T+6h: run inventory-query script (infra/tools/inv-query) for cross-region candidates; if >600 H100-equivalent available within 7d, start cross-region pull.
3) T+12h: if shortfall >500 GPU-weeks, start broker-lease negotiation and secure option for 1–2 weeks of capacity.
4) T+24h: if shortfall >1,200 GPU-weeks or broker options limited, place fast-ship order and activate premium shipping.
5) Post-event: capture realized lead times and update lane multipliers in procurement-sim repo.

Operational concerns and friction points observed in the sim runs:
- Compatibility losses when using brokered fleet (drivers, firmware, PCI versions) averaged 22% across SKUs unless pre-vetted.
- Cross-region transfers show a steady 0.4–0.6 week delay due to customs/logistics in APAC windows in real runs.
- Vendor fast-ship capacity often gated by monthly vendor caps; require pre-negotiated priority slots (we currently have one slot across two vendors).

Action items (owner,ETA):
- Pre-vet 3 broker vendors for H100/RMA compatibility (Samira, 2024-11-20).
- Negotiate and buy 2 fast-ship priority slots (Procurement, 2024-12-15).
- Add cross-region transfer SLA in runbook and automated inv-query filter (Noah, 2024-11-27).
- Add compatibility metadata to inventory DB (sku_firmware, pci_version) so broker compatibility can be estimated programmatically (Infra-Data, 2024-12-01).

Open questions (for leadership / procurement):
- How much premium budget are we willing to allocate monthly for guaranteed ~2-week replenishment (fast-ship)?
- Should we keep a rolling small buffer (200–400 H100-equivalent) reserved in a broker contract at all times?

End notes: this file is intended as a working simulation and on-call checklist. Numbers are estimates and should be re-run with current inventory snapshots before any procurement commitment. For the canonical simulation scripts and reproducible notebooks see linked_artifacts.

Decision log excerpt:
- 2024-10-10: initial concept approved by infra leadership (see JIRA-INFRA-301).
- 2024-11-01: first sim run seeded; found broker + fast-ship hybrid reduces 90th pct shortfall by ~45%.
